candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the Fort Worth and future 10X magnet facilities qualify on timing, cost, product mix, and customer certifications before the 2027 restriction window tightens.

candidates.theme_relation: Direct beneficiary of defense procurement restrictions, U.S. industrial policy, and efforts to reduce China-linked magnet and rare-earth dependency.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference/control name so smaller processors and feedstock suppliers can be compared against a known policy-backed leader.

candidates.theme_relation: Could benefit if policy and defense customers value domestic/allied separation capacity, heavy rare-earth oxides, and qualified non-Chinese feedstock flows.

candidates.node_relation: Strategic-minerals processor with direct antimony exposure; relevant to defense energetics, flame retardants, stockpile replenishment, and non-China/non-Russia supply concerns.

evidence.claim: Defense acquisition rules restrict procurement of covered materials mined, refined, separated, melted, or produced in covered countries, with key restrictions becoming effective January 1, 2027; China is listed as a covered country.
evidence.source_title: 48 CFR § 252.225-7052 - Restriction on the Acquisition of Certain Magnets, Tantalum, and Tungsten

evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a public-private partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense to accelerate an end-to-end U.S. rare-earth magnet supply chain and reduce foreign dependency.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense to Accelerate U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Independence

evidence.claim: MP Materials states that its Fort Worth Independence facility produces NdFeB permanent magnets and transforms refined rare-earth materials from Mountain Pass into metals, alloys, and finished magnets.
Energy Fuels says its White Mesa Mill is a U.S. rare-earth supply-chain link that processes monazite to produce rare-earth oxides for applications including drones and defense technologies.
Energy Fuels announced first U.S. primary production of terbium oxide at White Mesa and described planned production of Dy, Tb, and NdPr from monazite subject to approvals and sufficient feedstock.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels Announces First U.S. Primary Production of Critical Heavy Rare Earth Material in Decades

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels and Vulcan Elements announced a collaboration under which Energy Fuels agreed to supply initial quantities of high-purity light and heavy separated rare-earth oxides to Vulcan in Q4 2025.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels and Vulcan Elements Join Forces to Advance U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Security

evidence.claim: United States Antimony announced a five-year sole-source IDIQ contract with the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency for antimony ingots to replenish the U.S. National Defense Stockpile, with a stated value of $245 million.
evidence.source_title: United States Antimony Corporation Awarded $245 Million Sole-Source Five-Year Contract by the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency

evidence.claim: Perpetua Resources disclosed Defense Production Act Title III funding intended to advance construction readiness and permitting for the Stibnite project, which is tied to domestic antimony trisulfide capability for defense energetic materials.
evidence.source_title: Perpetua Resources Corp. Form 10-Q for quarter ended March 31, 2025

evidence.claim: Perpetua Resources announced EXIM financing approval for the Stibnite Gold Project and described the project as a source of antimony for American commercial and defense manufacturing.
evidence.source_title: Export Import Bank of the United States Approves Loan for Development of Perpetua Resources’ Stibnite Gold Project

memory_update.text: MP should remain the reference anchor for U.S. rare-earth mine-to-magnet capacity, but it is high-attention and should not dominate underfollowed discovery passes.

Energy Fuels is a priority underfollowed candidate for the separation/feedstock lane because White Mesa maps to monazite processing and separated rare-earth oxides rather than headline mining tonnage.

United States Antimony has unusually direct contract evidence for the strategic-minerals node via its DLA sole-source antimony ingot contract; verify order cadence and production economics in later layers.
Perpetua Resources is a regulated-asset and pre-production antimony candidate; keep as underfollowed but require permitting, financing, construction, and processing-path evidence before upgrading.
The node should be split in later work into at least four subnodes: rare-earth mine/separation, magnet alloy and finished magnets, antimony feedstock/processing, and defense qualification/compliance.

Need a separate scan for tungsten, graphite, samarium-cobalt magnet makers, recyclers, test/inspection labs, and private-to-public supplier relationships; this pass only captured the most evidence-backed U.S.-listed names.

node: Strategic minerals, rare-earth separation, and qualified magnet supply
summary: This pass expands the universe around the hypothesis that the investable chokepoint is not simply mining tonnage, but compliant feedstock, rare-earth separation, magnet qualification, and defense-grade specialty minerals. The clearest reference anchor is MP Materials because it maps directly to U.S. mine-to-magnet capacity and DoD-backed magnet independence. The underfollowed lane points to Energy Fuels as a rare-earth oxide/separation and monazite-processing bottleneck, United States Antimony as a defense-stockpile antimony processor with sole-source contract evidence, and Perpetua Resources as a pre-production antimony/gold project with DoD/EXIM-linked strategic funding. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
